title: Round-trip recovery of triple lists
statement: Fix a width $w \ge 1$, and let $ts$ be any finite list of triples $(p, d, m)$, where the position $p$ ranges over $\{0, 1, \dots, w-1\}$ and $d, m$ are Boolean flags. Converting $ts$ into an aux list of index–direction entries — appending a termination marker, the pair consisting of the out-of-range index $w$ together with the flag false, after each triple whose flag $m$ is true — and then parsing that aux list back into triples recovers exactly the original list $ts$.
hypotheses_covered: ts is an arbitrary finite list of triples (position in {0,…,w-1}, direction bit, marker bit)
replaced:
Round-trip identity: for every triple list $ts$, applying
$\mathrm{triplesToAux}$ and then $\mathrm{parseAux}$ recovers $ts$.
